pages.title: Payments rollback runbook
pages.storage:
Owner

Dana (Platform on-call lead)

Service

payments-api

Severity

Use during a SEV1 or SEV2 caused by a bad payments release

Jira

PAY-6 Safer payments deploys and rollbacks

Last reviewed

2026-10-14

When to use this runbook

Roll back when a payments-api release is live and at least one of these is true:

  • The charge success rate on the Payments overview dashboard drops below 97% for 5 minutes.

  • p95 latency on POST /v2/charges stays above 800 ms for 5 minutes.

  • Error logs show a spike that started within 30 minutes of the deploy.

If the release also ran a database migration, read Migrations below before step 2. A rollback does not undo schema changes.

Post in the incident channel before you start, and name yourself as the person rolling back. Only one person runs the rollback.

Steps

  1. Confirm the current and previous release. The previous revision is the one you are rolling back to.

    bash

  2. Run the rollback script from the root of the payments-api repo. ROLLBACK_TIMEOUT is in seconds and defaults to 300. Raise it to 600 if the cluster is under load.

    bash

    The script calls helm rollback payments 0 --wait, so it returns only when the previous release is ready or the timeout expires.

  3. Check that the pods are on the previous image tag and passing readiness.

    bash

  4. Watch the charge success rate for 10 minutes. It should be back above 99%.

  5. Freeze deploys: add the deploy-freeze label to the payments-api repo's open release PR and say so in the incident channel.

If the script times out

A timeout usually means the previous image cannot pull or a pod is failing readiness. Do not run the script twice in parallel.

bash

If a pod is stuck, delete it and let the deployment replace it. Then run step 2 again with a longer timeout.

Migrations

Payments migrations are expand-only for 1 release, so the previous release can run against the new schema. If the release notes say the migration was contract (dropped or renamed a column), page the database on-call before rolling back.

After the rollback

  • Open a follow-up in Jira under PAY-6 with the bad release tag and the dashboard screenshot.

  • Keep the freeze until the fix is reviewed by 2 people.

  • Fill in the incident timeline. See .

  • Write the new value to a file with mode 600. Never paste secrets into a terminal history or the incident channel.

Rotate the PSP API key

  1. Create a second key in the PSP dashboard. Both keys stay valid until you revoke the old one.

  2. Store it in Vault and restart the pods:

    bash /tmp/psp-key.txt ./scripts/rotate-secrets.sh --secret psp-api-key --value-file /tmp/psp-key.txt shred -u /tmp/psp-key.txt]]>

  3. Create a test charge in staging and check for 201.

  4. Revoke the old key in the PSP dashboard 1 hour later.

Rotate the webhook signing secret

The PSP signs every webhook with this secret. The PSP dashboard lets you keep the old secret valid for 24 hours, so set that before you rotate.

bash

Then watch for 401 signature_invalid responses on /webhooks/psp. A few during the restart are expected. If they continue for more than 5 minutes, see .

pages.title: Scale payment workers
pages.storage:
Owner

Dana (Platform on-call lead)

Service

payments-workers

Jira

PAY-17 Autoscale workers on settlement queue depth

Last reviewed

2026-10-21

When to use this runbook

The settlement workers normally scale themselves: a HorizontalPodAutoscaler keeps them between workers.min and workers.max on CPU. The autoscaler does not see queue depth yet (that is PAY-17), so scale by hand when:

  • The Pending settlement jobs panel stays above 5,000 for 10 minutes.

  • You expect a burst, such as a merchant batch import or the first hour after a PSP outage.

Limits

The chart sets the bounds. Stay inside them; going above the maximum needs a database review, because every worker pod opens its own connection pool.

yamldeploy/helm/values.yaml (excerpt)

Steps

  1. Check the current count and what the autoscaler wants:

    bash

  2. Pick a count. Rule of thumb: 1 worker per 1,500 pending jobs, at least 2, at most 8.

  3. Scale from the root of the payments-api repo. The script refuses counts outside the chart limits and waits for the rollout.

    bash

  4. Watch the pending jobs panel. It should fall within 15 minutes.

  5. When the queue is under 500, let the autoscaler take over again. It will settle back toward workers.min within about 5 minutes; you do not need to scale down by hand.

If the queue does not move

  • Workers are up but idle: check that settlement enqueue is not paused. See for the resume step.

  • Workers are failing: look for settlement batch failed in the worker logs. A PSP outage looks like this; follow .

  • Database connection errors: you are near the connection limit. Scale down to the previous count and page the database on-call.

pages.title: Fail over the payments database
pages.storage:
Owner

Dana (Platform on-call lead)

Service

payments-pg (Patroni, 1 primary and 2 replicas), payments-api

Jira

PAY-11 Payments database resilience

Last reviewed

2026-10-08

When to use this runbook

Patroni fails over on its own when the primary stops answering for 30 seconds. Use this runbook when it does not, or when you need a planned switchover (host maintenance, a stuck primary that still answers health checks).

A failover drops every open connection. Charges in flight return 500 and clients retry with the same Idempotency-Key, so no charge is created twice. Tell the incident channel before you start.

Connection budget

After a failover every pod reconnects at once. The new primary must accept all of them, so check the budget before and after any change to the pool size.

yamldeploy/helm/values.yaml (excerpt)

PAYMENTS_DB_POOL is the pool size per pod (see src/db/pool.ts). With 3 API pods and up to 8 worker pods that is 11 x 20 = 220 connections at the worst moment, against max_connections = 200 on payments-pg. Patroni reserves 20 for superuser and replication, so in practice the API reconnects first and some workers retry for up to 1 minute. This is expected. PgBouncer (PAY-13) will remove the problem.

Steps

  1. See the cluster state and pick the replica with the lowest lag as the candidate:

    bash

  2. Run the failover from the root of the payments-api repo. Add --force only if the primary is unreachable.

    bash

    The script promotes the candidate, then restarts payments-api and payments-workers so their pools connect to the new primary.

  3. Confirm the new leader and that replication is streaming to the remaining replica:

    bash

  4. Check that POST /v2/charges returns 201 again and the error rate is back to normal within 5 minutes.

  5. Rebuild the old primary as a replica: patronictl reinit payments-pg payments-pg-0. This takes about 20 minutes for the current data size.

Do not

  • Do not raise the pool size during an incident to "help" reconnects. It makes the connection storm worse.

  • Do not fail over across regions. There is no cross-region replica; see .

pages.title: Drain the settlement queue
pages.storage:
Owner

Dana (Platform on-call lead)

Service

payments-api, payments-workers

Jira

PAY-4 Async settlement worker

Last reviewed

2026-10-02

When to use this runbook

Drain the queue before anything that must not run while settlements are in flight:

  • A database failover that is planned, not forced.

  • A PSP maintenance window announced in advance.

  • A worker release that changes how settlement_jobs rows are claimed.

Draining does not stop charges. POST /v2/charges keeps accepting requests; their settlement jobs are created as held until you resume.

How it works

The API inserts a settlement_jobs row for every charge. Workers claim pending rows in batches with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Setting SETTLEMENT_ENQUEUE_PAUSED=true on the API makes new jobs held instead of pending; the workers keep going until no pending row is left.

Steps

  1. Note the current pending count on the Pending settlement jobs panel. Draining takes about 1 minute per 1,000 jobs with 4 workers.

  2. Start the drain from the root of the payments-api repo. The default timeout is 900 seconds.

    bash

    It prints the pending count every 10 seconds and exits 0 when it reaches 0.

  3. If it exits 1 (timeout), the workers are probably failing. Check the worker logs before you retry, and consider scaling up with .

  4. Do the maintenance.

  5. Resume. The script turns enqueue back on and releases every held job to pending. The backlog clears within a few minutes.

    bash

drain-queue.sh changes the deployment with kubectl set env. The next Helm release resets it to the chart value, so a deploy during a drain also resumes enqueue. Freeze deploys while draining.

pages.title: Replay failed PSP webhooks
pages.storage:
Owner

Priya (Payments engineer)

Service

payments-api webhook ingestion

Jira

PAY-20 Replay dead-lettered webhooks from the admin console

Last reviewed

2026-10-27

When to use this runbook

When a PSP webhook fails to process, payments-api still answers 200 (so the PSP stops retrying) and stores the event in webhook_dead_letters. Charges stay in settling until the event is replayed. Replay when:

  • The Webhook dead letters panel is above 0 for more than 15 minutes.

  • A merchant reports charges stuck in settling for more than 1 hour.

  • You have just fixed the cause of a processing error, such as a database outage.

A 401 signature_invalid is not a dead letter. It means the signing secret is wrong; see .

Steps

  1. See what would be replayed. Narrow it with --since to the start of the incident.

    bash

  2. Replay. The script posts each event to the internal endpoint POST /internal/webhooks/replay/:id, which applies it and deletes the dead letter. The default limit is 500 events per run.

    bash

  3. Run it again until it prints events: 0.

  4. Spot-check 3 replayed charges with GET /v2/charges/:id. They should be settled with a settled_at time.

Replay is safe to repeat

webhook_events has the PSP event id as its primary key, so a replayed event that was already applied is ignored. If a replay fails, the event stays in webhook_dead_letters and you can run the script again.

pages.title: PSP outage runbook
pages.storage:
Owner

Dana (Platform on-call lead)

Applies to

Outages or slowdowns at our payment service provider (PSP)

Last reviewed

2026-07-22

How a PSP outage looks

  • Charge success rate drops for every merchant at the same time, while our own latency stays normal.

  • Settlement falls behind and worker errors mention timeouts to the PSP.

  • Webhooks stop arriving, or arrive in bursts.

  • The PSP status page may lag by 15 to 30 minutes. Trust our dashboards first.

What to do

  1. Open a SEV2 (SEV1 if charges fail outright). Follow .

  2. Call the PSP support line. The number and our account ID are in the vendor contacts vault entry. Ask for an incident reference and put it in the incident.

  3. Do not roll back or fail over. Neither helps with a PSP outage, and both add risk.

  4. Tell the merchant success team. Merchants see declines with a generic error; they should not retry in a loop.

  5. When the PSP recovers, expect a burst. Scale up first: .

  6. Replay webhooks that failed during the outage: .

Known gaps

We do not yet hold settlement submissions while the PSP is degraded, so workers keep retrying and fill the logs. That work is PAY-16. Until it ships, expect noisy worker logs during an outage and ignore them.

After the outage

  • Ask the PSP for their incident report and attach it to our review.

  • Reconcile: compare the PSP settlement report for the outage window with our settled charges. Differences go to the finance channel.

What it does

payments-api takes card charges and refunds from Acme's checkout and merchant tools, sends them to our payment service provider (PSP), and records the result. It is the only service that talks to the PSP. The same image runs in 2 roles:

  • api (payments-api deployment, 3 pods): the HTTP API and PSP webhooks.

  • worker (payments-workers deployment, 2 to 8 pods): settlement. See .

The role comes from PAYMENTS_ROLE, set by the Helm chart.

pages.storage:

How a release ships

  1. A merge to main builds the image and tags it with the version in package.json.

  2. The release pipeline bumps image.tag in deploy/helm/values.yaml and runs helm upgrade in staging.

  3. After 30 minutes of clean staging metrics, a person approves the production step. Production runs the same command against prod-eu-west-1.

bashWhat the pipeline runs

What the chart creates

Template

Objects

deploy/helm/templates/workers.yaml

Both deployments get every key under env as an environment variable, plus the secrets from payments-secrets.

Values that matter in production

yamldeploy/helm/values.yaml (excerpt)

  • replicaCount: API pods. 3 covers peak traffic with 1 pod down.

  • workers.min and workers.max: bounds for the autoscaler and for manual scaling.

  • The pool size per pod. Any change here needs a check against the connection budget in .

pages.title: Settlement worker overview
pages.storage:
Owner

Lena (Payments engineer)

Deployment

payments-workers (same image as payments-api, PAYMENTS_ROLE=worker)

Jira

PAY-4 Async settlement worker

Last reviewed

2026-10-23

What it does

When a charge is created, the API writes a row to settlement_jobs and returns at once. The settlement worker picks those rows up and submits the charges to the PSP for capture. The PSP confirms with a charge.settled webhook, which marks the charge settled. The decision to move this out of the request path is .

Job states

Status

Meaning

pending

Waiting for a worker

held

Created during a drain; released by the resume step

submitted

Sent to the PSP, waiting for the webhook

How work is claimed

Each worker pod runs PAYMENTS_WORKER_CONCURRENCY slots (8 by default). Each slot claims up to SETTLEMENT_BATCH_SIZE rows (50) in one transaction:

sql

SKIP LOCKED means slots and pods never wait on each other, so adding pods adds throughput until the database becomes the limit. When a slot finds nothing to do it sleeps for 2 seconds.

Scaling

The HPA scales on CPU between 2 and 8 pods. Queue depth does not drive it yet (PAY-17). For bursts, follow .

Failure handling

  • If a batch fails, its transaction rolls back and the rows go back to pending for the next claim.

  • If the PSP never sends the webhook, the charge stays in settling. Dead-lettered webhooks are handled in .

Dashboards

  • Pending settlement jobs: alert at 5,000 for 10 minutes.

  • Settlement lag p99: target under 15 minutes.

pages.title: Webhook ingestion service overview
pages.storage:
Owner

Priya (Payments engineer)

Endpoint

POST /webhooks/psp on payments-api

Last reviewed

2026-10-27

What it does

The PSP tells us about charge outcomes by webhook. payments-api verifies each event, stores it once, and updates the charge. The handler is src/routes/webhooks.ts.

Verification

The PSP signs the raw request body with HMAC-SHA256 and sends the hex digest in the psp-signature header. We compute the same digest with WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET and compare in constant time. A mismatch returns 401 signature_invalid and nothing is stored.

bashSend a signed test event to staging

Processing

  1. Insert into webhook_events. The PSP event id is the primary key, so a duplicate delivery is ignored.

  2. For charge.settled, set the charge to settled with settled_at.

  3. If anything fails, store the event in webhook_dead_letters with the error, and still answer 200. The PSP retries non-2xx answers for 3 days, which would hide the problem; we prefer to replay ourselves.

Event types we handle

Type

Effect

charge.settled

Charge becomes settled

anything else

Stored in webhook_events only, for audit

Operations

  • Dead letters: .

  • Secret rotation: .

pages.title: Ledger service overview
pages.storage:
Owner

Lena (Payments engineer)

Team

Finance engineering, with Platform on-call

Last reviewed

2026-06-11

What it does

The ledger is the double-entry record of every money movement at Acme. Payments tells the ledger what happened; the ledger decides how it is booked. Finance reports, merchant payouts and the monthly close all read from the ledger, never from payments tables.

Accounts

Account

Debited when

Credited when

PSP receivable

A charge settles

The PSP pays out to our bank

Merchant payable

A merchant is paid out

A charge settles, net of fees

Fee revenue

A fee is refunded

A charge settles

Refunds clearing

A refund is issued

The PSP confirms the refund

Rules everyone relies on

  • Entries are append-only. A mistake is fixed with a reversing entry, never an update.

  • Every entry balances: total debits equal total credits, per currency.

  • Amounts are integers in minor units. There is no floating point anywhere in the ledger.

  • The ledger is eventually consistent with payments. A settled charge normally appears within 1 minute; the daily reconciliation catches anything that does not.

Reconciliation

Every night the ledger compares its PSP receivable with the PSP's settlement report. Any difference above 0.00 opens a ticket for the finance team. On-call is only paged if the job itself fails.

Who to ask

Questions about how something is booked go to Finance engineering. Questions about whether a payment happened go to the Payments team first.

pages.title: Fraud screening service overview
pages.storage:
Owner

Priya (Payments engineer)

Team

Risk, with Platform on-call for availability

Last reviewed

2026-05-28

What it does

Fraud screening scores every charge before we send it to the PSP. It answers in 3 ways: allow, review or block. Payments respects the answer; it never overrides a block.

Decisions

Decision

What happens to the charge

Share of charges (October)

Allow

Sent to the PSP as normal

97.8%

Review

Held for up to 4 hours for the Risk team, then allowed or refunded

1.9%

Block

Declined with a generic reason

0.3%

When screening is down

If screening does not answer within 300 ms, payments fails open for merchants on the low-risk list and fails closed for everyone else. Risk owns the list and reviews it every quarter. A fail-closed period shows up as a drop in charge success rate for some merchants only, which makes it easy to confuse with a merchant integration issue.

Signals

  • Card and device history across Acme merchants

  • Velocity: charges per card, per device and per IP in the last hour

  • Mismatch between billing country and IP country

  • Merchant category and the merchant's own dispute rate

Changing the rules

Rules change only through the Risk team's review. Payments engineers should not add exceptions for a merchant, even during an incident. Ask the Risk on-call instead.

pages.title: Payments codebase tour
pages.storage:
Owner

Marco (Payments tech lead)

Audience

Engineers in their first 2 weeks on Payments

Last reviewed

2026-10-16

How to read this

Open payments-api next to this page and follow a charge from the HTTP request to settlement. It takes about an hour. You should have finished first.

1. Start-up: src/server.ts

The process reads its configuration with loadConfig() from src/config.ts, creates the Postgres pool with createPool() from src/db/pool.ts, and builds a Router. Routes are attached in one place:

typescript

The HTTP server itself lives at the bottom of server.ts: it reads the body, matches the route, calls the handler and writes JSON. If PAYMENTS_ROLE is worker, no server starts and the settlement worker runs instead.

2. Routing: src/routes/index.ts

registerRoutes() calls one registerX() function per area: charges, refunds and webhooks. To add an endpoint, add it to the area's file; to add an area, add a file and call it from registerRoutes(). The router in src/http/router.ts is deliberately tiny: exact segments and :params, nothing else.

3. A charge: src/routes/charges.ts

  1. The handler checks the Idempotency-Key header, then validates the body with validateChargeRequest().

  2. withIdempotency() from src/idempotency.ts returns the stored response if the key was seen in the last 24 hours. The reasoning is in .

  3. The charge row and a settlement_jobs row are inserted, and the API answers 201 without waiting for the PSP.

4. Settlement: src/workers/settlement-worker.ts

startSettlementWorker() runs a loop per slot that claims jobs with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Read next to this file.

5. The PSP answers: src/routes/webhooks.ts

The charge.settled webhook closes the loop. Note how failures go to a dead-letter table instead of returning an error to the PSP.

Conventions

  • Money is always an integer in minor units, in SQL and in JSON. 12.50 EUR is 1250.

  • Handlers return { status, body }; they never touch the raw response.

  • Error bodies are { "error": "snake_case_code" }. Clients match on the code, so never reword one.

  • SQL lives next to the handler that uses it. There is no ORM.

pages.title: Platform on-call onboarding
pages.storage:
Owner

Dana (Platform on-call lead)

Audience

Engineers joining the Platform on-call rotation

Last reviewed

2026-09-04

How the rotation works

  • Shifts are 1 week, Monday 10:00 to Monday 10:00 CET, with a primary and a secondary.

  • The primary acknowledges pages within 5 minutes. The secondary takes over if the primary does not, and helps on any SEV1.

  • You are not expected to fix everything alone. Escalating early is part of the job.

Before your first shift

  1. Shadow 1 full shift with the current primary.

  2. Do 1 shift as secondary with an experienced primary.

  3. Read every page under Runbooks in this space, starting with .

  4. Run a rollback and a database failover in staging with a teammate watching. Staging is there for this.

  5. Check your access: production cluster read, Vault for payments, the incident tool and the status page.

During a shift

  • Hand over at the start: open incidents, ongoing changes, anything flaky.

  • Keep your laptop and a charger within reach. You do not need to stay home.

  • If you are paged more than twice in a night, the secondary takes the next morning's pages and you start late.

Runbooks are only useful if they are right

If a runbook step did not work as written, say so in the incident review and fix the page the same week. Every runbook has an owner on its first line; tell them if you change something important.

Compensation

On-call weeks are paid as agreed in the on-call policy from People Ops, plus time off in lieu for any night with more than 1 hour of work.

pages.title: ADR-009: Retire the v1 refunds API
pages.storage:
Status

Accepted

Date

2026-02-12

Deciders

Marco, Priya

Owner

Marco (Payments tech lead)

Jira

PAY-15 Remove the v1 refunds endpoint, fix version 2026.12

Context

v1 refunds only support full refunds, take amounts in a different field from the rest of the API, and have no idempotency. Support spends about 6 hours a month on refunds issued twice through v1. v2 refunds cover every v1 use case.

Decision

We retire POST /v1/refunds:

  1. Now: v1 answers with Deprecation and Sunset headers, and is only served when a feature flag is on.

  2. By 2026-11-30: every internal caller moves to POST /v2/refunds. Merchant success contacts the 9 merchants still on v1.

  3. Release 2026.12 (sunset 2026-12-15): the endpoint and its flag are deleted. Calls get 404.

Options considered

  • Keep v1 as a thin wrapper over v2. Rejected: the wrapper would still need its own tests and docs forever, and still could not offer idempotency without a client change.

  • Remove it at once. Rejected: 9 merchants need time to migrate.

Consequences

  • The Refunds API guide documents v1 only as a migration aid until the sunset.

  • After release 2026.12, a v1 call is a client bug, not an incident.

  • The removal ties into : after it, every money-moving endpoint is idempotent.

pages.title: ADR-012: Idempotency keys for charge creation
pages.storage:
Status

Accepted, implemented

Date

2026-03-04

Deciders

Marco, Priya, Dana

Owner

Marco (Payments tech lead)

Jira

PAY-2, PAY-3

Context

Checkout retries a charge when it does not get an answer within 10 seconds. Before v2, a slow database during peak hours caused duplicate charges: the first request was still running when the retry arrived. In February we refunded 214 duplicates by hand.

Decision

Every POST /v2/charges and POST /v2/refunds must carry an Idempotency-Key header of at least 8 characters. The server stores the key with a hash of the request body and the response it sent:

  • Same key, same body, within 24 hours: return the stored response with idempotent-replay: true. Nothing is created.

  • Same key, different body: 409 idempotency_key_conflict. This is almost always a client bug.

  • No key: 400 idempotency_key_required.

Keys live in the idempotency_keys table in the payments database, written by withIdempotency() in src/idempotency.ts.

sqlTable

Options considered

  1. Keys in Postgres (chosen). Same transaction boundary as the charge, no new dependency.

  2. Keys in Redis. Faster, but a Redis failover could forget a key and allow a duplicate. Duplicates are the exact problem we are solving.

  3. Deduplicate on the PSP side. The PSP supports it, but only per merchant account, and refunds would still be exposed.

Consequences

  • Clients had to start sending keys. We gave them 6 weeks and a 400 with a clear code.

  • A nightly job deletes keys older than 24 hours. The table holds about 2 million rows at peak.

  • v1 refunds do not support keys, one more reason to retire them. See .

pages.title: ADR-014: Async settlement worker queue
pages.storage:
Status

Accepted, implemented

Date

2026-05-19

Deciders

Lena, Marco, Dana

Owner

Lena (Payments engineer)

Jira

PAY-4, PAY-5

Context

Charges used to call the PSP capture API inside the HTTP request. When the PSP slowed down, our request threads filled up, latency on POST /v2/charges went above 3 seconds, and checkout timed out. The PSP was slow; we made it look like we were down.

Decision

Capture moves out of the request path. The API writes a settlement_jobs row in the same transaction as the charge and answers 201. A separate worker deployment claims jobs and talks to the PSP.

The queue is a Postgres table, not a message broker. Workers claim rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so many workers can run without coordination. The worker is src/workers/settlement-worker.ts.

Options considered

Option

For

Against

Postgres table with SKIP LOCKED (chosen)

Job and charge commit together. No new system to run.

Load on the main database. Fine up to roughly 500 jobs per second.

RabbitMQ

Built for this, good tooling

Needs an outbox to stay consistent with the charge. One more system for on-call.

Managed cloud queue

No operations work

Same outbox problem, and ties settlement to one cloud provider

Consequences

  • Charges are pending for seconds to minutes after 201. Merchants were told to rely on the charge.settled webhook, not the create response.

  • Settlement lag became a metric we watch, with an alert at 5,000 pending jobs.

  • Operations need new runbooks for scaling and draining. See and .

  • We revisit the broker option if we pass 300 jobs per second sustained.

pages.title: ADR-015: Active-passive multi-region database
pages.storage:
Status

Accepted, implementation planned for Q1 2027

Date

2026-09-10

Deciders

Priya, Marco, Dana, Lena

Owner

Priya (Payments engineer)

Jira

PAY-18 Multi-region active-passive database

Context

All of payments runs in 1 region. A regional outage would stop every Acme merchant from taking payments until the region recovers. Our largest merchants now ask for a recovery time objective of 1 hour in their contracts, and today we cannot promise it.

Decision

We will run the payments database active-passive across 2 regions:

  • The primary region keeps the Patroni cluster as it is today.

  • A standby cluster in the second region follows by asynchronous streaming replication.

  • Failing over to the standby region is a manual, rehearsed decision taken by the incident lead, never automatic.

  • Targets: recovery point objective 1 minute, recovery time objective 1 hour.

Options considered

  1. Active-passive with a manual switch (chosen). Simple to reason about. Asynchronous replication means a regional failover can lose up to about 1 minute of writes, which reconciliation with the PSP can recover.

  2. Active-active. Needs conflict handling for charges and refunds. Too risky for money movement.

  3. Backups restored in another region. Cheap, but a restore takes about 4 hours, which misses the target.

Consequences

  • Infrastructure cost for the database roughly doubles.

  • The failover runbook needs a regional section and a twice-yearly rehearsal.

  • Until this ships, a regional outage is handled as a long incident with the PSP's help. Contracts must not promise a 1-hour recovery time yet.

PAY-12 Refunds API v2

Last reviewed

2026-10-20

Overview

Use POST /v2/refunds for every new integration. It supports partial refunds and idempotency keys. POST /v1/refunds is deprecated and documented below only to help you migrate.

Create a refund (v2)

bash

Field

Type

Notes

charge_id

string

Required. The charge must be settled.

amount

integer

Required, in minor units. Several partial refunds are allowed while their sum stays at or below the charge amount.

reason

string

Optional: requested_by_customer (default), duplicate or fraudulent.

A successful call returns 201 with the refund in pending. It moves to succeeded when the PSP confirms, usually within 1 minute.

Errors

Status

Code

What to do

400

idempotency_key_required

Send an Idempotency-Key of at least 8 characters.

404

charge_not_refundable

The charge does not exist or is not settled yet. Retry after the charge.settled webhook.

409

idempotency_key_conflict

You reused a key with a different body. Use a new key.

422

amount_exceeds_refundable

The sum of refunds would pass the charge amount.

Migrating from v1

POST /v1/refunds stops working after release 2026.12. See and PAY-15.

bashv1 (deprecated)

v1

No idempotency

pages.title: Charges API guide
pages.storage:
Owner

Priya (Payments engineer)

Audience

Internal teams and merchants integrating card payments

Jira

PAY-1 Charges API v2

Last reviewed

2026-10-20

Create a charge

bash

Field

Type

Notes

amount

integer

Required. Minor units, 1 to 10,000,000 (100,000.00).

currency

string

Required. EUR, USD, GBP or RON.

source

string

Required. A tokenised card from checkout, starting with src_.

description

string

Optional. Shown to the merchant, not the cardholder.

Response

json

201 means we accepted the charge, not that the money moved. The charge goes pending, then settling, then settled. Listen for the charge.settled webhook, or poll GET /v2/charges/:id no more than once every 5 seconds.

Idempotency

Send a unique Idempotency-Key per logical charge and reuse it on every retry of that charge. Within 24 hours, a retry with the same key and body returns the original response with the header idempotent-replay: true. Background: .

Errors

Status

Code

Meaning

400

idempotency_key_required

Missing or shorter than 8 characters

409

idempotency_key_conflict

Key reused with a different body

422

amount_invalid, amount_too_large

Amount not a positive integer, or above the limit

422

currency_unsupported

Currency not in the list above

422

source_invalid

Source is not a checkout token

500

internal_error

Retry with the same key and exponential backoff

Limits

  • 50 charge requests per second per merchant. Above that you get 429 from the gateway.

  • Refunds have their own guide: .
